- [LLM extraction times out at 30s and SILENTLY falls back (benchmarks measure the wrong path)](temporalstore-llm-extraction-silent-fallback.md) - 2026-08-18 `9d2d4e19`. Extraction runs in `matrixark_batch_extract` NOT per-ingest (0.4s ingest = no LLM ran). Qwen 7B on CPU ~1.5 tok/s, minutes/call, so every call hit the 30s `MATRIXARK_EXTRACTION_TIMEOUT_SEC` and fell back while still reporting `understanding_provider: openai_compatible` - a full "Qwen" quality run made ZERO model calls. Cross-session recall is bounded by EXTRACTION not embeddings (encoder swap 5/8->6/8). Pack `defaults` omit per-item labels - apply them or cross-session items look unlabeled
- [mem0 search() returned EMPTY for every query + results weren't addressable](temporalstore-mem0-search-defects.md) - 2026-08-18 `4ad2a77c` + matrixarkai PR #50. Shim read `selected_refs`; packs now serve `groups[].items[]`. Existing tests used a FAKE gateway so they only tested request shaping. METHOD: sweep every API (39 MCP tools + 11 mem0 methods) against the REAL gateway; most first-round failures are wrong ARGS - check `required` in matrixark_mcp_schemas.py

[resource .claude/projects/C--Users-user--claude/memory/MEMORY.md #1]
- [Context memory -21.6% + TWO levers that proved UNSAFE as defaults](temporalstore-context-memory-bounding.md) - 2026-08-18 `4ad2a77c`. I reported -65% before finding the problems. Skipping event-less-node summaries removed EVERY node_l1 + the profile summary layer; sharing serving route/scope objects makes a module fail 7/20 runs (0/20 on main), unexplained. HAZARD: a failed `cd` into a worktree ran `git reset --hard` on ANOTHER session's branch
- [Per-tenant memory policy (live+durable) + per-session/per-tenant index budgets](temporalstore-tenant-memory-policy.md) — 2026-08-17 merged bjmeetsfo main `5be533ad`. Every memory knob resolves per tenant (tenant→env→default), changeable on a RUNNING service via `matrixark_set_tenant_policy` (immediate + durable record), hot-reloaded policy file, or replayed records. Budgets are per SESSION (256) + per TENANT (2048), NO store-wide total (a global budget lets one tenant evict another). Eviction is recall-aware (event→segment→node→entity→summary) — that's what makes a tight budget affordable: 881→453 postings @40 turns, recall 5/5 (cliff at 128). Segments default OFF (-9%, a segment's text IS its event's); embeddings declinable per tenant (-16.2%, nothing dropped). GOTCHAs: scope keys are `|`-separated; served records carry only the tenant HASH so policies register under id AND hash

[resource .claude/projects/C--Users-user--claude/memory/MEMORY.md #2]
- [mem-opt phase3 (index growth bound) + phase4 (pipeline-task collapse, -25% resident)](temporalstore-memory-phase3-phase4.md) — 2026-08-17 merged bjmeetsfo main `5f53a66d`. Phase-3: summary rollup tombstones redundant per-event `context_index` postings (`MATRIXARK_INDEX_COMPACT_ON_SUMMARY`, default ON, -27.9% postings @40 turns, recall 5/5); per-scope cap + hard ceiling are default-OFF ON PURPOSE (a binding cap cost recall 5/5→4/5 — lever 1 already removed everything redundant). Phase-4 ROOT CAUSE: `matrixark_async_pipeline_task` = 26-30% of RESIDENT memory from DUPLICATION (193 rows / 25 task_hash, re-stamped every summary refresh, no latest-value key) → collapse to newest per (task_hash,status) = -25.2% whole-store resident. TRAP: plain latest-value collapse on task_hash empties retrieval's `extraction_committed` scan — 4 consumers disagree on "latest". Census: embeddings only 0.9% of logical bytes (quantization NOT worth it); next candidates `context_batch_commit` + `context_extraction_audit` (~18%, ~20KB/rec)
- [WSL rebuilt 2026-08-17 + WSL git auth via Windows GCM](wsl-rebuild-and-git-auth.md) — distro wiped (repo/AWS CLI/keys gone); restore recipe, and the lesson: an UNPUSHED branch is not backed up — phase-3 work was lost that way

[resource .claude/projects/C--Users-user--claude/memory/MEMORY.md #3]
- [Shared sync-write FLATTENED + raft fsync fix (live-proven)](temporalstore-write-path-flatten.md) — 2026-08-17: shared /execute sync-write 13.6ms/70qps/collapsing → 4ms/~2000qps/FLAT. Root cause was per-write O(n) WAL full-file scans (stats() per write engine.rs:503 + append rescan/N6a), NOT the manifest (#44 catalog-fold runs dump-time only — don't misattribute). Fix stack (gated default-OFF): TS_PHASE1_FLAT (O(1) seq cache, feat/phase1-oconst) + TS_ENGINE_CONCURRENT_COMMIT (lock-release across fsync, merged 58ca2539+PR#37) + TS_GROUP_COMMIT. Residual = global shards lock ~2000qps → per-shard split (#50). Raft: feat/raft-fsync-coalesce (idle storm 200/s→0, C≥4 collapse fixed, 42→11 fdatasync); residual 11 = apply-path fsyncs (#48)
- [Context-record memory ~74% reduction (interning+pruning+count-reduction)](temporalstore-memory-model-optimization.md) — 2026-08-17: root cause was storage_route/storage_options (61% of bytes, 5/14 distinct, stamped per-record) + ~15 constant internal index dimensions — NOT the caps (non-binding). Phase-1 interning+dim-pruning ~68% (`5d27125c`), Phase-2 count-reduction −24.9% (`267cb500`); scope_key-intern/buffer-prune REVERTED (unsafe). Phase-3 index-growth bound (temporal compaction+cap+ceiling) in flight. All gated default-ON + correctness-gated. matrixarkai review via oss-review-all branch

- [mem0 full parity + native scope-forget + TTL/keyed-upsert SHIPPED](temporalstore-mem0-parity-and-delete.md) — 2026-08-17: complete mem0 drop-in (get/update(supersede)/history + delete/forget/get_all/reset, search+add reshaped to mem0 shape) + provenance-closure delete + physical purge `4bf34652`; Rust-native WAL-committed scope-forget `714a362b`/`17398c2e` (recovery-safe); per-record TTL/retention-cutoff + keyed-upsert(truth-rank guard) `a676c35d`. All independently re-verified regression-free; matrixarkai PR #36 refreshed to `a676c35d`. GOTCHAs: proxy_impl tests run `--bin matrixark_rust_proxy` not `--lib`; base main has ~90 pre-existing failures (verify by diffing failing-test-NAME sets vs pristine main). KNOWN GAPS (not fixed): delete-before-extract leak (async race), audit-trail residue post-purge (GDPR), local O(n) delete scan
